tested_scope: Exactly one deterministic self-local claim/idempotency fixture continuing c24. Logical operation O5 and payload digest D5 retain old provider identity I5 and new identity I6. Provider-side evidence M56 authoritatively and immutably maps I5 and I6 to one execution-domain key K5. The fixture tests the minimum additional invariants under which the prior terminal no-effect proof P_I5 may be reused for the I6 claim, while repository finalization still uses fresh fence F7 CAS plus exact readback. No concrete provider, public source, O/downstream/other-worker state, shared ledger, scheduler state, hosted compute, richer-mode arbitration, finite quota, or second semantic leaf is tested.

minimum_provider_side_invariants: M56 immutably binds O5,D5,I5 and I6 to the same provider execution-domain key K5.
All identities bound to K5 are aliases over one shared attempt set A(K5); no identity-local subnamespace can create an attempt outside A(K5).
P_I5 resolves to K5-domain evidence: it proves A(K5) is complete, contains no irreversible effect, and K5 is permanently sealed/quiescent rather than merely sealing the I5 spelling.
Alias creation or identity rotation cannot reopen K5, allocate a replacement execution domain, or append attempts after the permanent K5 seal.
fixture.repository_freshness_invariant: Final negative closure of the current I6 claim still requires current F7 compare-and-swap and exact repository readback; provider-domain equivalence does not replace repository claim freshness.
fixture.candidate_action: Reuse P_I5 as provider-side terminal no-effect evidence for the I6 claim only when all four provider-side invariants are evidenced, then finalize only through current F7 CAS/readback.
fixture.reason: Under the stated invariants, I5 and I6 are two names for the same immutable sealed attempt domain K5. P_I5 therefore covers the entire shared attempt set A(K5), and I6 cannot introduce an unseen provider attempt or reopen execution. F7 CAS/readback independently preserves current repository-claim authority. Removing either the domain-wide proof/seal scope or the no-reopen/no-subnamespace invariant reintroduces an execution path not covered by P_I5.

weak_rule_falsified.rule: An authoritative mapping that says I5 and I6 share one execution-domain key is by itself sufficient to reuse an I5 terminal no-effect proof for I6.
weak_rule_falsified.falsification: The mapping alone does not establish that P_I5 sealed the domain rather than only an identity-local attempt subset, nor that a new alias cannot append or reopen attempts. Cross-identity reuse therefore additionally requires domain-wide attempt-set/proof scope and monotonic no-reopen semantics.

fixture.minimum_safe_rule: Cross-identity terminal-proof reuse is safe only if exact evidence binds both identities to one immutable execution domain, all aliases share one complete attempt set, the terminal proof and permanent seal are scoped to that domain, alias rotation cannot create/reopen execution, and current repository claim finalization independently passes fresh-fence CAS/readback.

observations: Provider identity equivalence is not a single predicate: domain-key equality, attempt-set equality, proof scope, and seal monotonicity are distinct requirements.
A provider-domain proof can survive idempotency-identity rotation only when the proof target and sealing semantics are domain-wide rather than identity-local.
Repository fence freshness remains orthogonal to provider execution-domain equivalence.
inference: Within this exact fixture, the minimum safe reuse contract is the conjunction of immutable same-domain mapping, one shared attempt set, domain-scoped complete no-effect plus permanent seal, no alias-triggered reopen/new-domain semantics, and fresh F7 repository CAS/readback. Same-domain mapping alone is insufficient.
